extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients, institutional grants administrators, PD/PIs, Authorized Organization Representatives (AORs), and Grants Management Officials (GMOs)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedural requirements for administering NIH grant awards, including transfers of awards, organizational status changes, prior approvals, funding adjustments, data/publication rights, and resource sharing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient organization — paper application required components
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed new recipient organization must provide the GMO with a change of institution application which may be submitted using the PHS 398 or PHS 416-1 paper application forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper application should include, at a minimum: PHS 398 Face Page; Budget pages (current and future years) (or narrative budget information for modular awards); Other Project Information and Senior/Key Personnel components; updated biographical sketches for PD/PI and existing senior/key personnel and biosketches for any proposed new senior/key personnel; progress report if transferring on the anniversary date and statement whether research plans/aims have changed; updated other support pages if necessary; Resources page including probable effect of the move; Checklist page; Certification of IRB/IACUC approval (including OHRP and OLAW assurance numbers, if applicable); detailed list of equipment purchased with grant funds to be transferred (inclusion indicates acceptance of title).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient organization — electronic application required components
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitted electronically via Grants.gov using the Parent Announcement, the proposed recipient's application must include specified SF 424 (R&R) components and other materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic application should include: SF 424 (R&R) Cover Component; SF 424 (R&R) Project Performance Site Location(s); SF 424 (R&R) Other Project Information including certification of IRB/IACUC approval (with assurance numbers if applicable), Facilities and Other Resources (including probable effect of the move), and detailed list of equipment to be transferred; SF 424 (R&R) Senior/Key Person Profile with updated biosketches and other support pages as necessary; Budget pages applicable for activity code (use R&R Detailed Budget form if original award was modular); PHS 398 Research Plan (including progress report if transferring on anniversary date and statement on whether plans/aims have changed); PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement; PHS 398 Checklist; and, as applicable, PHS Training Budget Form, PHS 398 Career Development Award Supplemental Form, PHS 398 Research Training Program Form, PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trial Information Form, SBIR/STTR Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of relinquishing statement does not guarantee transfer approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of a relinquishing statement by NIH does not guarantee approval of a transfer application for continued funding of a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may request additional information necessary to review the request; transfer approval is a separate decision and NIH may adjust funding as part of grant closeout and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of revised Notice of Award (NoA) for transfers and funding adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will accomplish a change of recipient organization by issuing a revised NoA to the original recipient reflecting revised budget/project period end dates, deletion of future-year support, and deobligation of remaining funds, and will issue a NoA to the new recipient reflecting the direct cost balance reported on the relinquishing statement plus applicable indirect costs if funds are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transfer occurs on anniversary date, NoA to new recipient will reflect previously committed direct cost level plus applicable indirect costs if funds available. If during a budget period, awarding IC policy will determine whether NoA to new recipient reflects direct cost relinquished or total costs relinquished; amount may be adjusted downward as a result of closeout. Deobligation is based on estimated expenditures through relinquishment date or PMS balance, whichever is less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award costs for transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may, at its own risk and without NIH prior approval, incur obligations and expenditures to cover costs before the beginning date of a transfer award if necessary to conduct the project and would not require prior approval under an awarded grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For transfers, pre-award costs are treated like non-competing continuation awards and are not limited to 90 days prior to the beginning date of the initial budget period of the transferred award to the new recipient organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice required for change in organizational status (merger, SII, name change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must give NIH advance notice of organizational status changes such as Merger, Successor-in-Interest (SII), or Name Change to ensure continued legal/administrative ability to meet NIH obligations and to avoid payment interruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients encouraged to contact lead NIH awarding IC GMO to explain nature of change and receive guidance on whether treated as name change or SII; NIH reserves right to review materials and make independent determination. Formal request should be submitted as soon as possible so NIH can determine eligibility and take necessary action in advance of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor-in-Interest (SII) — required letter contents and supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For an SII, a letter signed by the AORs of the transferor and transferee must be sent to the lead NIH awarding IC and must include specified statements and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter must: stipulate transfer will be properly effected in accordance with applicable law; indicate transferor relinquishes all rights and interests in affected grants; request award records be modified to reflect transferee as recipient; state effective date; provide transferee's EIN and, if new, completed Form W-9; include verification of transferee's compliance with applicable requirements (e.g., research misconduct assurance); include a list of all affected NIH grants (active and pending) with for each: complete grant number, PD/PI name(s), current budget period and project period, total direct costs (as originally recommended) plus applicable indirect costs for each remaining budget period, and if SII during budget period, estimated current-year direct and indirect costs remaining as of SII effective date (may be reported on PHS 3734 or as attachment). Also include a complete face page (PHS 398) for each affected grant signed by an AOR at the transferee, and copy of current negotiated indirect cost rate agreement for transferee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission option for SII materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may submit an electronic application for a successor-in-interest request via Grants.gov using the Parent Announcement to satisfy requirements for face pages, EIN confirmation, transferee compliance verification, and Relinquishing Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submission is acceptable in lieu of separate paper face pages and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferee eligibility for recognition as SII
rubrics_metrics.description: To be recognized as the SII, the transferee organization must meet each grant program's eligibility requirements (except for SBIR/STTR programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon review and acceptance of information, NIH will revise the NoA(s) to show the transferee as recipient of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name change notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For name changes, the recipient's written notification to the lead NIH awarding IC must include the effective date of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised face pages are not required for name changes because they are reported and processed with the next award action (e.g., non-competing continuation award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval required for deviations from NoA terms and NIHGPS restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH prior approval is required for any deviation from terms or conditions stated or referenced in the NoA, including those in the NIHGPS, and includes undertaking any activities disapproved or restricted as a condition of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should assume that any change inconsistent with award terms requires prior approval and consult the GMO when uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a foreign component to a grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding a non-monetary foreign component under a grant to a domestic or foreign organization requires NIH prior approval; NIH will not accept nor approve requests to add a foreign subaward to an ongoing project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to add foreign activities should be submitted for NIH review prior to undertaking; foreign subawards to ongoing projects are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-amount subaward permissibility and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: With NIH prior approval, a pass-through entity may provide subawards based on fixed amounts (as defined in 2 CFR Part 200.201), up to $500,000, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) negotiate fixed amount using cost principles or other pricing data; project scope must have specific measurable goals/objectives and available pricing/historical/unit data to establish fixed budget; (2) budget determined by subrecipient proposal, pricing data, and cost principles; (3) accountability based on performance/results and reported via reporting tool in written subaward and to NIH in annual RPPR; (4) no routine monitoring of actual costs and subrecipients not required to submit FFRs, but record retention and audit access requirements (2 CFR 200.334-338) still apply; (5) payments based on meeting specific Federal award requirements—possible methods include partial milestone payments, unit price payments, or single payment at completion; (6) must not be used in programs requiring cost sharing; (7) may generate/use program income but requirements for program income (deduction/addition/cost-sharing) do not apply; (8) at end of fixed amount award, subrecipient must certify project completed or identify uncompleted activities and that expenditures complied with 2 CFR 200.403; where activities not completed, Federal award amount must be reduced to reflect uncompleted activities; (9) periodic reports may be established; (10) prior approval requirements that apply are found at 2 CFR Part 200.308(f) (specified paragraphs) and §200.333. Distinguish fixed-amount subaward vs fixed-rate agreement: fixed-rate (negotiated cost per unit where total unknown at creation) generally does not require prior approval provided no other factors require NIH prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional NIH funding during current budget period (non-competing supplement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for additional funding for a current budget period to meet increased costs within the scope of the approved application but unforeseen when the application or progress report was submitted is a non-competing supplemental application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests must be submitted electronically for single and multi-project awards and are not required to compete with other applications. When calculating award for additional funds, NIH will (1) prorate funding if requested budget is adjusted at time of award, and (2) use the institution's current indirect cost rate (the rate in effect when new funding is provided). Other recipient-initiated requests that change scope may be required to compete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional NIH funding with extension of final budget period
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a non-competing extension of the final budget period with a minimal amount of additional funds should be submitted to the GMO in writing at least 30 days before the project period is scheduled to expire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually requests are for up to 12 months and must be for work that remains or for orderly phase-out with resources available. Request must specify proposed revised ending date and justify extension and additional funds; special justification needed if extension would exceed 12 months. NIH will not approve extensions primarily to permit use of unobligated balances. All award terms and conditions apply during extension. Note fiscal close-out rule (31 U.S.C. §1552(a)): recipients must report disbursements on FFR no later than August 31 of the fifth fiscal year after year of availability; after five years funds are cancelled and returned to Treasury which may limit NIH ability to extend final budget period with funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting of trainee costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebudgeting amounts previously awarded for trainee costs (stipends, tuition, and fees) to other categories of expense requires NIH prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This excludes trainee travel (not considered a trainee cost) and training-related expenses. Special rules may apply for institutional training grants (see other sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting between construction and non-construction work
rubrics_metrics.description: Under awards that provide for both construction and non-construction work, NIH prior approval is required to transfer funds between the two types of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any transfer between construction and non-construction budget categories requires prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of research grant funds when a K award is issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds budgeted under an NIH grant for an individual's salary and fringe benefits that become available as a result of that individual receiving a K award may not be used for any other purpose without NIH prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must obtain NIH approval before reallocating such funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for prior approval — general procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Most requests for NIH awarding IC prior approval must be made in writing (including e-mail) to the GMO no later than 30 days before the proposed change and signed by the AOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If e-mailed, must provide evidence of AOR's approval (a cc to the AOR is not acceptable). SBIR/STTR recipients must submit all prior approval requests through the eRA Commons Prior Approval Module. A request by a subrecipient is addressed to the recipient who will review and approve/disapprove in writing; recipients will not approve revisions inconsistent with the award. PD/PI signature no longer required for submission but recipient must secure and retain such signature for each prior approval request and make it available upon request (applies to all PD/PIs when multiple). Email requests must be clearly identified as prior approval, include complete grant number in subject line, be sent by AOR to the GMO that signed the NoA, and include identifying info for recipient, initiating PD/PI, and AOR (phone, fax, email). GMO will review and provide response to AOR with copies to PD/PI and cognizant NIH PO; only GMO responses are valid. Recipients are encouraged to consult GMO when uncertain. Under consortium agreement, pass-through entity usually has prior approval authority but may not approve actions inconsistent with purpose or terms of NIH grant; if a consortium participant's action will result in a change requiring NIH approval, pass-through entity must obtain awarding IC approval before approving participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR special prior approval rules for adding subawards post-award
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR and STTR recipients are required to seek prior approval when adding a new domestic subaward to a project post-award if arrangement was not originally part of the peer reviewed and approved application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreign risk assessment is required for the entity selected for the subaward when prior approval request is submitted via updated SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Form in eRA Commons. The recipient must receive official written approval from the NIH Grants Management Official prior to signing a subaward agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in data, publication and copyrighting
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, recipients own the rights in data resulting from a grant-supported project and may copyright publications and other copyrightable works developed under an NIH grant, except as otherwise provided in the award terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this purpose, 'data' includes recorded information in any media (writings, films, software, statistical records, etc.). NIH must be given a royalty-free, nonexclusive, and irrevocable license for the Federal government to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the material and to authorize others to do so for Federal purposes. Students/fellows under educational awards also may assert copyright. Journal or other copyright practices are acceptable unless they prevent the recipient from making copies for its own use (2 CFR 200.315) or from complying with NIH policies including the NIH Public Access Policy. Disposition of royalties and income addressed elsewhere (Program Income rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of Federal funding (Stevens Amendment) and disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: All recipients must acknowledge Federal funding when issuing statements, press releases, requests for proposals, bid invitations, and other documents describing projects or programs funded in whole or in part with Federal money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgment must include: (1) statement of NIH grant support with specific grant number and percentage/dollar amount of total costs financed with federal funds (and non-governmental funds if NIH program requires cost-sharing), e.g., recommended wording provided in policy; and (2) disclaimer: 'The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health.' If issuing a press release about NIH-supported research, notify the NIH funding component in advance for coordination. Publications resulting from NIH-funded work must be included in annual or final progress reports with URL or PMCID; if not available electronically, one copy of the publication may be provided with the progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Public Access Policy — submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the NIH Public Access Policy, NIH-funded investigators are required to submit (or have submitted for them) to PubMed Central (PMC) an electronic version of the final, peer-reviewed manuscript upon acceptance for publication, to be made publicly available without embargo upon the Official Date of Publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author Accepted Manuscript (author's final version accepted for journal publication including all revisions from peer review and all associated tables/graphics/supplemental material) must be submitted for any manuscript accepted on or after July 1, 2025 that resulted from NIH funding (in whole or in part) via grants/cooperative agreements/contracts/Other Transactions/NIH intramural research/official work of NIH employee. Institutions and investigators are responsible for ensuring compliance. Applicants citing NIH-funded articles that fall under the Policy and were authored/co-authored by the applicant must include the PMCID or NIHMS ID. More details at NIH Public Access Policy webpages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of unique research resources and research tools
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH considers sharing unique research resources developed with NIH funds an important means to enhance the value of sponsored research; recipients are expected to make such resources readily available for research purposes to qualified individuals after associated findings are accepted for publication or after provided to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff oversee resource sharing policies and assess adequacy of resource sharing plans. NIH Research Tools Policy provides principles/guidelines and implementation suggestions. For biological materials, NIH has procedures allowing recipients to retain and license biological materials for which patent protection might not be pursued. Terms of licensing/distribution must reflect Bayh-Dole objectives. Upon request by awarding IC, recipient must provide copy of documents or sample material developed under award and may charge nominal shipping fee (income treated as program income). Investigators may distribute materials through their lab/org or submit to repositories (e.g., ATCC) ensuring those entities distribute consistently with NIH Research Tools Policy. Investigators are expected to submit unique biological information (DNA sequences, crystallographic coordinates) to appropriate data banks and include pertinent information on nature, quality, or characterization of materials when distributing.
